title: Experiment Gateways and Rescue Protocols (working draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight working draft defining the 'experiment gateway' concept and an actionable rescue protocol for cross-functional canary / A/B rollouts across Redwood products. The focus is operationalizing early-stop signals, rapid partial isolations, and clear human handoffs so that experiments can be both safe and fast.

Why a gateway?
- Many canaries fail not because the model is catastrophically wrong, but because secondary systems (caching, routing, telemetry) interact with the variant in unexpected ways. The gateway is an explicit set of pre-flight and live checks that sit between 'release' and full exposure.

High-level flow (summary):
1) Pre-flight gateway (automated): schema checks, latency budget smoke, model compatibility, eval pass on fixed prompt-set, quota checks, linked infra capacity verification. If any automated gate fails -> block exposure and notify stakeholders with the failure reason.
2) Soft-launch gateway (10–100 unique users): enable variant behind feature flag / slice, synthetic pressure tests + production-sampled traffic. Monitor saved signals for 30m.
3) Observation window: defined metrics (latency p95, error rate, negative-sentiment delta, regen-rate) evaluated against thresholds and trends. Use rolling 5/15/60m windows.
4) Ramp decisions: increment based on signal pass and runway (preapproved ramp schedule). If borderline, hold and trigger human review.
5) Rescue protocol: quick-isolate -> partial rollback -> full rollback with comms.

Pre-flight checklist (owners):
- Product: hypothesis, key metrics, target slices, expected failure modes (owner: Product PM).
- Eng: infra capacity sign-off (Dedicated pools), feature-flag plan, fragmentation testing (owner: Release Eng).
- SRE: alerting configuration, runbook pointers, canary dashboards (owner: SRE lead).
- Security/Compliance: data path review if private data used (owner: Security).
- CS (if customer-facing): customer comm plan + opt-out list (owner: Customer Success).

Important signals to include in the gateway (examples):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 and token-throughput delta
- Error rate (5xx, model failures, timeouts) and retry-churn
- Cost anomaly (per-request token cost up >20% compared to baseline)
- Quality regressions: eval score on canary prompt set, user satisfaction signal (if available), semantic-change index (measures distribution shift of top tokens)
content_continued:
Rescue protocol (quick reference):
- Tier 0: Immediate rollback thresholds (automated): 5xx > 1% for 5m OR latency p95 > 2x baseline for 3m OR security trigger -> AUTO FULL ROLLBACK + INCIDENT CHANNEL ping (#rr-incident).
- Tier 1: Quarantine slice: if early signal localized to single cohort, shift that slice to baseline model and keep rest running. Notify experiment owner and oncall.
- Tier 2: Canary freeze + introspect: hold ramps, start forensics (logs, traces, model logits if enabled). Use the canary-runbook template (linked).
- Tier 3: Full rollback and postmortem if persistent, notify stakeholders, open postmortem ticket (JIRA).

Escalation ladder and communications templates:
- 1st responder (SRE oncall): post short status to Slack channel #rr-canaries with subject line: [CANARY ALERT] <experiment> - <short reason> and initial action (quarantine/rollback).
- Product owner: send customer note draft if external users impacted.
- Engineering manager: coordinate hotfix or patch rollout to baseline.
- Exec notify if SLA breach or major revenue/enterprise impact.

Minimal telemetry contract (what the gateway must surface):
- Human-readable rapid dashboard: 3 lines: (1) experiment name + slice %; (2) live status with autocounter (ok/warn/fail); (3) top 3 signals with delta vs baseline and short link to trace.
- Raw export: last 24h event logs for the canary, token-level cost × count, audit logs for feature flag changes.

Operational playbook (walkthrough):
- PRE-LAUNCH (T-48h): confirm pre-flight passes, upload canary prompt set, schedule SRE slack observability window (2 hours).
- LAUNCH DAY: 09:00 enable soft-launch slice 0.1–1% depending on risk. Let it run 30–90 minutes. If all green, follow ramp schedule.
- IF WARNING SIGNAL: immediate 1) freeze ramp, 2) apply quarantine if slice-localized, 3) run 15m synthetic replay, 4) convene triage call (15m).
- ROLLBACK: toggle feature flag to baseline, validate via smoke queries, close the traffic gate only after smoke passes.

Checklist for a postmortem draft (post-rollback):
- Timeline of events (timestamps), owner actions, signal graphs, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, follow-ups (tests to add to pre-flight), and next steps for stakeholders.

Open questions / decisions to make (TODOs):
- Define canonical set of quality evals for every experiment type (chat vs rerank vs embeddings).
- Where to store canary prompt sets and who curates them? (Suggestion: repo under /rollouts/canary-prompt-sets).
- Frequency of audit drills for rescue protocol (quarterly?).
- Policy on automatic vs manual rollbacks for Dedicated customers with contractual SLAs.

Quick notes to self (working fragments):
- Consider 'circuit-breaker' that auto-reduces batch sizes / threads before full rollback to salvage throughput.
- Add 'synthetic adversarial probe' to pre-flight for language models (simple prompt fuzzers).
- We need a single Slack shortcut to 'quarantine-slice' that triggers the flag change and posts to channels.

Notes: this is intentionally terse and operational. Put comments here if you want sections expanded into separate docs (pre-flight tests, quarantine CLI, dashboard mock).

Sign-off: draft for review by cross-functional stakeholders. Tagging folks here as collaborators for feedback.
